question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{3}{2},$ find $\text{E}[2Y-4X].$

current_example.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274274/assets/8ed1db1f24035c09d79b37a63060eb9dcacb50dbdfdae8f899b7a28b78513e82.svg)

Find the expected value of $Y.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The marginal density function for $Y$ when $y \geq 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{x}^{3}{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{{y}^{3}}{lim}_{b\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{b}\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{{y}^{3}}{lim}_{b\to \infty }{[-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}]}_{1}^{b} \\  & =\frac{4}{{y}^{3}}{lim}_{b\to \infty }(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2{b}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{4}{{y}^{3}}(\frac{1}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{2}{{y}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for $f_Y(y)$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274274/assets/f2eaf65338e3188fe2931d637a38cc02d63b86e1e948a30832dbf910c3ebaf54.svg)

Finally, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }y\cdot \frac{2}{{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2{lim}_{b\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{b}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2{lim}_{b\to \infty }{[-\frac{1}{y}]}_{1}^{b} \\  & =2{lim}_{b\to \infty }(1-\frac{1}{b}) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
